Pre-Incorporation & Know-Your-Customer

UBO transparency, Apostille authentication chain, official name clearance restricted wordlist, and pre-incorporation statutory fee budget.

UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, por el que se aprueba el Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010; Real Decreto 10/2021, de 25 de mayo, por el que se crea y regula el Registro Central de Titularidad Real; supplemented by EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843 as transposed.
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

For a standard SL, a virtual office is acceptable only as a correspondence address; the statutory domicile must be a physical location in Spain where central administration or the principal establishment is situated, per art. 9 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital. For a licensed payment institution under the Spanish transposition of PSD2, a virtual office is impermissible: a tangible physical office, local management, and auditable compliance infrastructure in Spain are mandatory.

✓ Partner licensed company-secretary channels provide local registered address and government mail forwarding.

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central (for name certification) and the relevant Registro Mercantil Provincial (for inscription of the company in the commercial registry).

Governing statute

Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital, Articles 20, 22, 30, and 62.

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura de constitución otorgada ante notario, filed with the Registro Mercantil Provincial.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 12 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

EUR 3,000 minimum share capital, fully subscribed and paid-up in cash at incorporation. The funds must be deposited in a Spanish credit institution and the resulting blocking certificate is required before the notarial deed is executed; the block is released upon registration in the Commercial Registry.

Funding & unlock path: Fire safety certification under the Technical Building Code Basic Document SI (Seguridad en caso de incendio); municipal activity license or responsible declaration for the office premises; occupational risk prevention plan and workplace health and safety assessment; structural load verification for IT and server equipment; electrical installation and lightning protection inspection; emergency evacuation plan and civil defense clearance in accordance with local fire brigade requirements.

Paid-in capital rule: EUR 3,000 minimum share capital, fully subscribed and paid-up in cash at incorporation. The funds must be deposited in a Spanish credit institution and the resulting blocking certificate is required before the notarial deed is executed; the block is released upon registration in the Commercial Registry.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including the Sede Electrónica de la AEAT. Spanish tax identification numbers are administered through the Registro de Operadores Económicos and the census of taxpayers. Regional tax authorities generally do not administer ordinary national corporate income tax or VAT registration for entities established in Spain.

E-government filing portal

A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a Número de Identificación Fiscal (NIF) by filing Modelo 036 with the AEAT. A provisional NIF may be requested after execution of the incorporation deed and before registration with the Mercantile Registry; the definitive NIF must be obtained after registration by submitting the registered deed and updated corporate information within the applicable filing period. The NIF normally uses the Spanish legal-entity format beginning with the letter B for an ordinary Spanish limited liability company. A foreign entity without a Spanish establishment obtains an NIF through Modelo 036, directly or through an authorized representative, providing constitutional documents, evidence of legal existence, registered address, identification of directors or legal representatives, and proof of authority. Foreign documents may require apostille or legalization and an official Spanish translation. VAT registration is generally performed through the same census filing. An entity carrying out intra-Community transactions should apply for inclusion in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios (ROI) and obtain a VAT number activated for VIES purposes. A Spanish VAT number is generally the NIF prefixed by ES. Additional registrations may be required for the Immediate Supply of Information system (SII), the monthly VAT refund register (REDEME), or other sectoral tax obligations.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a Número de Identificación Fiscal (NIF) by filing Modelo 036 with the AEAT. A provisional NIF may be requested after execution of the incorporation deed and before registration with the Mercantile Registry; the definitive NIF must be obtained after registration by submitting the registered deed and updated corporate information within the applicable filing period. The NIF normally uses the Spanish legal-entity format beginning with the letter B for an ordinary Spanish limited liability company. A foreign entity without a Spanish establishment obtains an NIF through Modelo 036, directly or through an authorized representative, providing constitutional documents, evidence of legal existence, registered address, identification of directors or legal representatives, and proof of authority. Foreign documents may require apostille or legalization and an official Spanish translation. VAT registration is generally performed through the same census filing. An entity carrying out intra-Community transactions should apply for inclusion in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios (ROI) and obtain a VAT number activated for VIES purposes. A Spanish VAT number is generally the NIF prefixed by ES. Additional registrations may be required for the Immediate Supply of Information system (SII), the monthly VAT refund register (REDEME), or other sectoral tax obligations.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation

Available election forms

Spain has no general United States-style check-the-box election for a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada. The SL is ordinarily subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax as a separate legal taxpayer. Available elections or optional regimes may include tax consolidation for qualifying corporate groups, the special regime for mergers and other corporate reorganizations, the special regime for entities engaged in leasing housing, the VAT cash-accounting regime where eligibility conditions are met, and certain investment or holding-company regimes. A Spanish SL is not ordinarily eligible to elect transparent treatment merely by filing an election. Spanish anti-hybrid mismatch rules may deny deductions, impose inclusion, or otherwise neutralize mismatches involving hybrid entities, instruments, or imported arrangements. The payment-services activity may also require authorization or registration as a payment institution, electronic-money institution, or other regulated provider under Spanish and European payment-services legislation; tax registration does not substitute for financial-regulatory authorization.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

EUR 0 for ordinary domestic taxable activity: Spain generally has no general turnover threshold below which an established business is automatically exempt from VAT registration. A person carrying out an independent economic activity must register in the taxpayer census before commencing taxable activity, subject to applicable place-of-supply rules and exemptions. A separate EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold applies to certain intra-Community distance sales and electronically supplied, telecommunications, broadcasting, and similar services supplied to EU consumers, unless the supplier opts for destination taxation or uses the One Stop Shop. The threshold is not a general Spanish VAT-registration exemption.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Exports of goods from the Spanish VAT territory to destinations outside the European Union may qualify for the 0% VAT exemption with a right to deduct input VAT where the supplier or an authorized customer transports or dispatches the goods outside the EU and the export is substantiated by customs evidence and proof of exit. Intra-Community supplies of goods may qualify for exemption where the customer is identified for VAT in another EU Member State, the goods are dispatched to that Member State, the supplier reports the transaction correctly, and transport and customer-status evidence are retained. Services supplied to business customers established outside the EU may be outside the scope of Spanish VAT under the business-customer place-of-supply rule, subject to use-and-enjoyment restrictions and special rules for services connected with immovable property, events, transport, telecommunications, financial services, and other categories. Financial and payment services may also be VAT-exempt under specific statutory provisions, but exemption classification must be determined transaction by transaction; a payment gateway is not automatically entitled to treat all processing, technical, platform, or ancillary services as exempt. Export treatment requires contemporaneous evidence of customer status, contractual scope, payment flows, destination, transport or use, and the applicable place-of-supply rule.

  • Electronic export declaration filed through the Spanish customs system, including the Movement Reference Number (MRN)
  • Commercial invoice and contract or order documentation identifying the supplier, customer, goods, value, and delivery terms
  • Transport evidence, such as bill of lading, airway bill, CMR consignment note, courier record, or equivalent logistics evidence
  • Customs exit confirmation or equivalent electronic proof that the goods physically left the EU customs territory
  • Packing list and, where relevant, export licenses, permits, certificates of origin, and product-specific regulatory documents
  • Evidence of the purchaser's non-EU establishment or VAT status where relevant to the exemption
  • Accounting records, VAT ledgers, payment and settlement records, and reconciliation between invoice, customs declaration, and receipt
  • For offshore services: contract, customer tax-residence or business-status evidence, service-delivery records, platform or usage logs where relevant, and evidence supporting the applicable place-of-supply rule
  • Inward remittance evidence may support commercial and audit substantiation but is not generally a universal statutory condition for Spanish VAT export exemption

Spain does not currently operate a universal real-time pre-clearance system for every VAT invoice. Taxpayers within the mandatory SII regime, including qualifying large businesses with turnover exceeding EUR 6 million, VAT groups, REDEME entities, and voluntary participants, must transmit specified VAT ledger information electronically to the AEAT, generally within four calendar days, excluding certain holiday adjustments. Electronic invoicing and invoice-content rules are governed principally by Spanish invoicing legislation, including Royal Decree 1619/2012. Certified billing systems must preserve integrity, traceability, accessibility, legibility, and anti-tampering controls under the applicable requirements introduced by Law 11/2021 and Royal Decree 1007/2023, with implementation dates subject to subsequent regulatory amendments. The forthcoming B2B electronic-invoicing framework under the Create and Grow Law requires technical and procedural implementation before becoming generally operative. A payment gateway should maintain invoice, transaction, settlement, merchant, customer-location, chargeback, refund, and VAT-rate evidence capable of supporting place-of-supply and audit controls.

Spain has no general foreign-exchange rule requiring export proceeds to be repatriated within 180 days. Export proceeds may remain abroad subject to ordinary accounting, anti-money-laundering, payment-services, transfer-pricing, financial-reporting, and beneficial-ownership requirements. If a zero-rating or exemption is unsupported, the AEAT may assess output VAT retrospectively, deny or claw back input-VAT recovery, impose late-payment interest, and apply penalties under the General Tax Law 58/2003 and VAT Law 37/1992. Tax penalties for inaccurate or fraudulent tax treatment commonly range from 50% to 150% of the improperly avoided or unduly refunded tax, depending on the statutory classification, with aggravation for concealment, fraudulent means, or repeated conduct. False customs declarations may trigger customs debt, recovery of duties and taxes, customs penalties, and seizure or other measures under the Union Customs Code and Spanish implementing rules. Material intentional VAT fraud may also create criminal exposure under the Spanish Criminal Code, including liability where the defrauded tax quota exceeds the applicable criminal threshold. Refunds obtained without entitlement are recoverable with interest, and repeated unsupported export claims may result in heightened audit, denial of refund procedures, and referral to customs, financial-intelligence, or payment-services regulators.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain uses the euro and is subject to the EU single-market framework. The euro is fully convertible for ordinary current-account transactions, including trade payments, service fees, dividends, interest and other lawful remittances. Spain has no general exchange-control approval requirement for ordinary inbound or outbound payments. Capital-account transactions, shareholder loans, intercompany financing, acquisitions and disposals are generally permitted but may trigger statistical, foreign-investment, tax, beneficial-ownership, anti-money-laundering or sector-specific reporting. Profit remittance normally requires distributable accounting profits, approval of annual accounts and the distribution resolution, satisfaction of legal-reserve requirements, solvent payment capacity, proper withholding-tax analysis and maintenance of supporting books and records. Payments involving sanctioned parties, opaque ownership, unusual payment chains, unlicensed payment activity or inadequate source-of-funds evidence may be blocked or delayed by banks. A payment gateway must not confuse unrestricted euro convertibility with permission to provide regulated payment services without the required Banco de España authorization or passporting status.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Spain has no statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. Exporters may retain foreign-currency proceeds, subject to banking, accounting, tax, sanctions and anti-money-laundering controls. There is no general statutory deadline requiring conversion of export proceeds into euros. The company must retain commercial invoices, contracts, customs or delivery evidence where applicable, settlement records and reconciliation evidence. Banco de España statistical reporting may apply to relevant cross-border transactions or external liabilities under applicable reporting instructions and thresholds; these reporting obligations do not constitute a mandatory surrender or conversion rule. Physical cash or bearer negotiable instruments transported into or out of the EU at EUR 10,000 or more, or equivalent, are subject to EU cash-declaration requirements. Banks may impose contractual conversion, documentation or settlement requirements under their risk policies.

Central bank supervision: European Central Bank and Banco de España, with anti-money-laundering supervision and suspicious-transaction reporting administered by the Executive Service of the Commission for the Prevention of Money Laundering and Monetary Offences (SEPBLAC). Payment institutions and electronic-money institutions are principally supervised by Banco de España under the Spanish transposition of the EU Payment Services and Electronic Money frameworks.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Medium for operational payments and treasury diversification, but low as a substitute for a fully integrated Spanish banking relationship. An offshore digital EMI cannot lawfully provide regulated payment services to or from Spain solely because it offers an online account. The provider must be authorized in its home EEA state and validly passport services into Spain, or hold the relevant Spanish authorization. Customer funds must be safeguarded under the applicable payment-services or electronic-money regime and must not be used as ordinary corporate working capital. An EMI account may lack cash services, Spanish domestic lending, capital-escrow functionality, reliable correspondent access, card-scheme acquiring capability or support for high-risk merchant flows. A payment gateway operating merchant acquiring, payment initiation, money remittance, account-information, issuance or acquiring functions must map each activity to the applicable PSD2 authorization, electronic-money authorization, agent, outsourcing and safeguarding requirements. Direct Fedwire access is generally unavailable to an EU corporate or non-US EMI and normally requires a US correspondent or regulated payment partner.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

The stated activity is online merchant acquiring, clearing or payment processing, but the applicant cannot demonstrate the applicable Banco de España authorization, EEA passport, regulated partner arrangement or clearly limited technology-services role.

Root cause: The stated activity is online merchant acquiring, clearing or payment processing, but the applicant cannot demonstrate the applicable Banco de España authorization, EEA passport, regulated partner arrangement or clearly limited technology-services role.

Defense evidence: Authorization or passporting evidence; regulatory perimeter memorandum; business-flow diagram; funds-flow and safeguarding map; copies of regulated-partner agreements; outsourcing and sub-processing schedule; merchant-acquisition contracts; compliance officer appointment; AML and sanctions policies; transaction-monitoring methodology; complaints and safeguarding procedures.
Unclear ultimate beneficial ownership, nominee shareholders, layered offshore ownership, bearer-style documentation or inconsistent ownership information across corporate records.

Root cause: Unclear ultimate beneficial ownership, nominee shareholders, layered offshore ownership, bearer-style documentation or inconsistent ownership information across corporate records.

Defense evidence: Certified constitutional documents; current commercial-register extracts; ownership chart to natural-person beneficial owners; passports and residential-address evidence for directors, shareholders and UBOs; trust or foundation documents where applicable; notarized powers of attorney; written explanation of control rights; independent corporate-secretarial certification.
Non-resident ownership and directors combined with a Spanish registered office but no credible local management, employees, technology, compliance function or operating rationale.

Root cause: Non-resident ownership and directors combined with a Spanish registered office but no credible local management, employees, technology, compliance function or operating rationale.

Defense evidence: Business plan; Spanish office lease or service agreement with substance explanation; employment or contractor agreements; organization chart; board minutes; local compliance arrangements; technology architecture; projected transaction volumes; target-market analysis; customer and merchant onboarding policy; tax-residency and permanent-establishment analysis.
Expected high-volume cross-border flows, rapid pass-through of funds, Latin American corridors, nested payment relationships or merchant activity involving high-risk sectors.

Root cause: Expected high-volume cross-border flows, rapid pass-through of funds, Latin American corridors, nested payment relationships or merchant activity involving high-risk sectors.

Defense evidence: Country and corridor risk assessment; merchant underwriting standards; prohibited-business list; enhanced due-diligence policy; sample merchant files; transaction-monitoring scenarios; velocity and exposure limits; chargeback and fraud controls; sanctions-screening configuration; reconciliation reports; reserve policy; independent compliance testing plan.
Incoming shareholder capital or intercompany funding does not match the capital structure, stated purpose or sender identity, or is routed through unrelated third parties.

Root cause: Incoming shareholder capital or intercompany funding does not match the capital structure, stated purpose or sender identity, or is routed through unrelated third parties.

Defense evidence: Capital-increase or shareholder-loan agreement; board and shareholder resolutions; bank statements showing source of funds; audited or management accounts of the funder; tax-residency certificates; ownership evidence; beneficial-owner declarations; payment instruction identifying the legal purpose; Spanish accounting entries; related-party pricing analysis.
Expected transaction volumes are inconsistent with the company’s incorporation stage, stated revenue model or declared source of funds.

Root cause: Expected transaction volumes are inconsistent with the company’s incorporation stage, stated revenue model or declared source of funds.

Defense evidence: Three-year financial model; signed customer or merchant contracts; acquiring-bank or processor agreements; invoices; payment-volume forecast by country and currency; liquidity plan; capital adequacy and safeguarding calculations; explanation of seasonality; independent accountant confirmation.
Sanctions, politically exposed person, adverse media, fraud, cybercrime or high-risk-country exposure involving owners, directors, merchants, payers, beneficiaries or correspondent institutions.

Root cause: Sanctions, politically exposed person, adverse media, fraud, cybercrime or high-risk-country exposure involving owners, directors, merchants, payers, beneficiaries or correspondent institutions.

Defense evidence: Identity-resolution report; documented false-positive analysis; PEP and sanctions screening results; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; enhanced due-diligence approval; beneficial-owner declarations; contractual representations; escalation and exit criteria; evidence of ongoing monitoring.
Use of personal accounts, unregulated wallets, offshore virtual IBANs or unrelated third-party accounts for company receipts or merchant settlement.

Root cause: Use of personal accounts, unregulated wallets, offshore virtual IBANs or unrelated third-party accounts for company receipts or merchant settlement.

Defense evidence: Formal treasury policy; approved account list; segregation-of-funds procedures; bank-account ownership evidence; reconciliation controls; payment approval matrix; regulated-provider contracts; written explanation of historical transactions; remediation plan and independent control sign-off.
Incomplete Spanish tax, corporate or beneficial-ownership records, including missing NIF, outdated commercial-register information or inconsistent registered-office details.

Root cause: Incomplete Spanish tax, corporate or beneficial-ownership records, including missing NIF, outdated commercial-register information or inconsistent registered-office details.

Defense evidence: Spanish NIF certificate; deed of incorporation; registered commercial-register extract; beneficial-ownership declaration; powers of attorney; tax registration evidence; registered-office proof; annual filing calendar; accountant or gestor certification; updated director and shareholder register.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Route equity through a bank account in the name of the Spanish SL using SEPA Credit Transfer for euro funding or SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA currencies. The remitter should be the shareholder, parent or documented lender identified in the corporate records; third-party funding should be avoided unless legally documented and pre-cleared. The payment reference should state the legal purpose, such as share-capital contribution, capital increase, shareholder loan or intercompany loan, and must identify the relevant agreement or resolution. For an incorporation or formal capital increase, obtain the bank’s capital-deposit certificate where required by the notary or registry process; after registration, transfer funds to the operating account under the bank’s instructions. For a shareholder loan, retain the executed agreement, maturity, interest, repayment terms, transfer-pricing support and beneficial-owner evidence. Provide source-of-funds and source-of-wealth documentation, sender and beneficiary tax identifiers, ownership records and expected-use information. There is no universal Spanish FX purpose-code regime equivalent to a mandatory conversion code for ordinary commercial wires; banks may nevertheless require internal purpose categories, LEI, invoice references, VAT data, counterparty details and supporting documents. Reconcile every inbound transfer to the general ledger and investigate rejected, returned or mismatched payments.Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the SEPA scheme, subject to bank limits and sanctions screening. Use SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA commercial wires, with complete originator, beneficiary, intermediary-bank, invoice, purpose and Ultimate Beneficial Owner information. Use documentary commercial letters of credit issued or confirmed by a bank under UCP 600 where counterparty, country or performance risk justifies documentary settlement; align the invoice, transport documents, insurance, inspection certificate and beneficiary details precisely with the credit. Documentary collections may use URC 522 where appropriate but provide less payment certainty than a confirmed letter of credit. Use bank guarantees or standby letters of credit only with appropriate wording, collateral and authorized-bank review. Fedwire is a US domestic wholesale settlement system; the Spanish SL will normally access it through a US correspondent bank, regulated payment institution or treasury bank rather than directly. Maintain a payment matrix requiring dual approval, sanctions screening, invoice or contract support, segregation of duties, beneficiary verification, callback controls for changes to bank details and daily reconciliation. Avoid routing merchant funds through personal accounts or unrelated third-party accounts. For regulated payment activity, segregate and safeguard customer funds separately from corporate operating liquidity and document settlement timing, chargebacks, reserves and reconciliation.Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with a regulated bank, supported by documented underlying exposure, approved counterparty limits, ISDA or bank master terms, valuation controls and accounting treatment.Non-deliverable forwards where the relevant currency or jurisdiction does not permit practical delivery, subject to bank eligibility, local-law restrictions, documented commercial exposure and settlement through regulated counterparties.Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for documented recurring funding or balance-sheet exposures, subject to EMIR-related reporting, clearing, margin, collateral and risk-management requirements where applicable.Foreign-exchange swaps for short-term liquidity management and settlement-date mismatches, subject to treasury policy and counterparty limits.Plain-vanilla currency options or collars for documented exposures, subject to suitability, premium, valuation, collateral and accounting controls.Permitted euro and foreign-currency deposits or multicurrency accounts with regulated banks, with written limits on open positions and liquidity concentration.The company should not use derivatives for unapproved speculation, should document the hedged item and risk objective, and should confirm that any payment-service, safeguarding, prudential, accounting and regulatory capital restrictions do not prohibit the proposed hedge.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Medium for operational payments and treasury diversification, but low as a substitute for a fully integrated Spanish banking relationship. An offshore digital EMI cannot lawfully provide regulated payment services to or from Spain solely because it offers an online account. The provider must be authorized in its home EEA state and validly passport services into Spain, or hold the relevant Spanish authorization. Customer funds must be safeguarded under the applicable payment-services or electronic-money regime and must not be used as ordinary corporate working capital. An EMI account may lack cash services, Spanish domestic lending, capital-escrow functionality, reliable correspondent access, card-scheme acquiring capability or support for high-risk merchant flows. A payment gateway operating merchant acquiring, payment initiation, money remittance, account-information, issuance or acquiring functions must map each activity to the applicable PSD2 authorization, electronic-money authorization, agent, outsourcing and safeguarding requirements. Direct Fedwire access is generally unavailable to an EU corporate or non-US EMI and normally requires a US correspondent or regulated payment partner.

Turnover: Independent statutory audit is generally mandatory where the company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total assets exceeding EUR 2.85 million, annual net turnover exceeding EUR 5.7 million, or average employees exceeding 50. Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25%

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

25 days after fiscal year-end (e.g., 25 January for calendar-year entities ending 31 December)

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Box 1 / Line 1a (Taxable base) Net taxable income after adjustments, deductions, and incentives For Spanish SL with foreign branches or permanent establishments, include attributable income; non-residents file Modelo 210 with Spanish WHT obligations 100-600 EUR per day of delay (max 6 months); additional 0.4% monthly interest on unpaid tax; criminal sanctions for fraudulent filings

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: 6,000,000 EUR annual turnover

Economic substance scope: Spain's Law 11/2021 (ESR) requires demonstrable real economic activities, adequate employees, assets, and risks; non-compliance triggers recharacterization and penalties

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax Evasion

Statutory sanction: Criminal penalty: imprisonment 6 months to 6 years, fines equal to 100% of evaded tax, plus restitution

Director personal liability: Personal criminal liability, disqualification from corporate offices, and joint restitution obligations
Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance

Statutory sanction: Administrative fines 5,000-50,000 EUR per violation; potential 100% adjustment of transfer prices

Director personal liability: Personal fines and disqualification if willful misconduct
Economic Substance Violation

Statutory sanction: Recharacterization of income, fines up to 1,000,000 EUR, and license suspension

Director personal liability: Personal liability for fines and potential criminal sanctions for fraudulent substance claims
AML and Sanctions Breach

Statutory sanction: Fines up to 2,000,000 EUR, license revocation, and criminal prosecution

Director personal liability: Personal criminal liability, travel bans, and disqualification
Improper Profit Repatriation

Statutory sanction: WHT penalties 100% of unpaid tax plus 0.4% monthly interest; possible criminal evasion charges

Director personal liability: Personal restitution and disqualification from management
